review.brief_reason: The rewrite is algebraically valid as a real rational identity ((2r+(mom/q^2+2r)/q)/q^2 = (mom+2q^2*r*(q+1))/q^5, and log(log(sqrt(q))) = log(log(q)/2) for q>0), but it is not equivalent under gplearn protected semantics. Merging nested protected divisions into a single division by q^5 changes when the |denominator|<=0.001 guard fires: q^2 exceeds the threshold for |q|>~0.0316 while q^5 stays below it until |q|>~0.2512, so for 0.0316<|q|<=0.2512 the original divides normally while the proposal returns 1. Additionally the last term differs for 1e-6<|q|<=1e-3: log(log(sqrt(q))) evaluates the inner log on sqrt(|q|)>0.001, while log(q) is protected to 0.
review.counterexample: q=0.1, mom=1, r=1: original inner fraction (2r+(mom/q^2+2r)/q)/q^2 = 102200 (all divisions execute), but proposed (mom+2q^2*r*(q+1))/q^5 triggers protection since |q^5|=1e-5<=0.001 and returns 1; totals original ~148.05 vs proposed ~19.88. Second independent case: q=1e-4, mom=1, r=1 gives original last term log(log(sqrt(q)))=log(ln(0.01))~1.526 while proposed log(log(q)/2)=log(0/2)=0, totals ~-2.132 vs ~-0.606.
